passages.provision_quote: The Secretary of the California Health and Human Services Agency shall research, develop, and pursue discussions of a waiver framework in consultation with the federal government with the objective of creating a health care system that incorporates the following features and objectives:
passages.note: The operative section orders research, a waiver framework and reports, and the findings state the goal the research serves.

rows.reasoning: SB 770 (2023-2024), which Wiener authored and voted Aye on, directs the Health and Human Services Secretary to "research, develop, and pursue discussions of a waiver framework" and to report back; it enacts no financing system, so it is a study directive and cannot seat a chair. Its text does state the outcome it seeks — "the Legislature endorses a health care system with unified financing, such as a single-payer health care system" — which shows a side (toward public financing) without choosing between "Make healthcare free and available to everyone, fully paid for by the public sector" and "Make sure everyone has affordable coverage through a mix of public programs and regulated private insurance". The bill's own features list keeps cost sharing only for "essential services and treatments" and names Medicare, Medi-Cal and employer-sponsored insurance as systems whose disparities are to be identified, so it does not match the "fully paid for by the public sector" clause either.
needs_source: A California record whose operative section itself establishes or funds a unified/single-payer financing system (bill text plus Wiener's author line or roll call), rather than directing research toward one
